summary: Eighteen findings: one high, eleven medium, six low. The extraction is thorough and its 80 recorded mistakes hold, but the review's changes left defects. It removed D07 without replacing it, so D08 (and D09, D18) are stated with the condition E1 shows is ill-defined (high). The authors' 'very good' correction does not reach the abelian-type chain S36–S48, and S08/S09 keep the hypothesis E58 corrects. The 105 items the review added are disconnected from the dependency graph. Theorem 0.4 has no item; M10 repeats the false step of E29. Missing or mis-planned foundations: the GL lattice-chain local model and its Grassmannian embedding, the Grassmannian and flag schemes (planned at R09.1 but not cited), P05's claim that GS.1 plans the affine Grassmannian over a p-adic field and twisted affine flag varieties, and π_1(G) and the Kottwitz map (planned at BG1, which the report attributes to ReductiveGroupsPartII). The trace formula needs the geometric Frobenius, and Proposition 4.3.7's level-change input has no item. The lows are stale references, a duplicated misprint, three new misprints and two duplicate owners.
checked: Independence. PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-18 was written by Codex session codex-c83e7a (issue #1460, checkpoint PR #1684) and completed by Claude Code session cc-fb70e5 (PR #2014); REV-PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-18 was written by Claude Code session cc-2aeb03 (issue #1461). The string cc-f805bf occurs in none of the four target files (.result.json, .md, .review.json, reviews/REV-PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-18.md). Disclosure: this session wrote FIX-RT-AREA-automorphic-1 (automorphic/Shimura stages such as AA.4 and the ALS layers) and PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20 (routes to SmoothRepresentationsPartII and ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups). No finding touches those stages or routes; finding 18 concerns a different Part II id (SmoothRepresentationsPartIIParahoricCenters), and PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20 plans no Iwahori–Hecke centre, Kottwitz map or Lang theorem.

Source, fetched 30 September 2026: the published Numdam PDF (https://www.numdam.org/item/10.1007/s10240-018-0100-0.pdf, 98 pp., printed page = PDF page + 120), SHA-256 e2b4a0763f216be82da950f4c0dd2800adea8a0d911b12bfacf2b7e493b4618b, matching the extraction; arXiv:1512.01149 (v1 3 Dec 2015, v2 21 Dec 2015, v3 12 Apr 2018; v3 PDF SHA-256 7577bb3ea98e42949160deb8ad94710a48ef14f02ca7cc3949b6884a0d29f55e) used only for comparison. All findings refer to the published text. Errata: Crossref has no correction record for doi:10.1007/s10240-018-0100-0; the authors' corrections are in Kisin–Pappas–Zhou (read at arXiv:2409.03689v3, §§1.3.1–1.3.2, 6.1, 7.2–7.3). Pappas–Zhu arXiv:1110.5588v4 re-fetched (SHA-256 cbb879126ff50a5431e06046edd55d1da3ee4d260ddd4d80202a043e21b18b27, matching the extraction's pz13 archive), §9.c–9.d read.

The whole paper re-read against the text layer and 200–400 dpi page images, in seven parallel section passes (Introduction and §§1.1–1.2; §§1.3–1.4; §2; §§3.1–3.2; §§3.3–4.3; §§4.4–4.6; §4.7 and references). Every finding filed was re-checked personally at its page, and the counterexamples in findings 2, 11 and 14 were re-derived.

Items: all 275 statements compared with the paper by section. Faithful apart from the findings: G01–G15, R01–R07, U01–U13 (except U04, U06), M01–M13 (except M10), D01–D31 (except D08, D09, D18), S01–S51 (except S08, S09, S14 and the very-good gap of finding 3), N01–N14 (except N02, N10, N14), A01–A03 and the 105 added cited-input items (content faithful; graph wiring is finding 5). The intro results 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 0.6 are represented with matching hypotheses (S44/S46, S45, S49/S50, N05, N14); 0.4 is not (finding 4). Main-theorem hypotheses checked: p > 2, abelian type, tame splitting, p ∤ |π_1(G^der)| only in 4.6.23(2) and Thm 0.4/4.7.11, no D^H in (4), G unramified with x'_2 in (5), no E_8 in 1.4 and 3.3.

Recorded mistakes: E1–E80 each checked at its locator. All hold as recorded, with these remarks: E17 can be sharpened (finding 14); E3's locator is incomplete (finding 3); E65 duplicates E64 (finding 16); E41 re-derived (z = p − V(1) ∈ Ŵ(O_K) has ghost vector (p,0,0,…) and kills E([π])); E43, E46, E51, E58, E59, E70, E72 re-derived; E29 and E33 re-derived, with their consequences for M10 and missing items (findings 6, 7).

Library statuses: all 22 declarations cited under `baseline` (14 library items) opened at the pinned commits (Mathlib 082e2d3, Tau Ceti f790474) and exist with the stated scope, e.g. TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Reductive/Basic.lean:70,78; Mathlib/RingTheory/WittVector/Isocrystal.lean:79 (requires IsDomain, CharP, PerfectRing, as L02 says); TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AbelianVariety/Basic.lean:94; TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/FundamentalDomain.lean:232; TauCeti/GroupTheory/Coxeter/Bruhat.lean:156. Searched declarations.tsv for items marked missing (Grassmannian, GSp/symplectic group, Isocrystal, p-divisible, Dieudonné, display, Shimura, Hecke algebra, Weil restriction, parahoric, building, Kottwitz, henselization, nearby cycles, Cohen–Macaulay, affine Grassmannian, Néron, minuscule): Mathlib's Module.Grassmannian (functor only) is the only relevant hit (finding 8); the 620 Tau Ceti 'Minuscule' declarations are E6/E7 minuscule-weight Lie-algebra constructions, not the minuscule lattices of R01–R07.

Planned statuses: stage texts read for P01 (RG2.2), P02 (RG2.3), P03 (RG2.0a), P05 (GS.1, finding 9), P08 (R07.2), P09 (R07.4), P10 (R09.6), P12 (PELModuli M1, M2), P13 (ShimuraVarieties V1, V6, V8), N01 (LPV.0), N07 (SR.1), A03 (A4), moret-bailly-integral-points (PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R23.1). All except P05 plan the item in the paper's generality; P04 cites Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups Layer 9. Also read R09.1, BG0, BG1, SR.0–SR.6, LPV.1, A2, A6, SF.0, SF.1, RG2.0–RG2.5 and GS.0.

Routes and owners: the 10 routes, their stages and briefs; compared with the routes of PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-ZHOU-26, KISIN-ZHOU-25, KISIN-17, KISIN-MADAPUSIPERA-SHIN-22, VANHOFTEN-24, GLEASON-LIM-XU-26, ZHU-17, SCHOLZE-WEINSTEIN-20, HE-18, CESNAVICIUS-22, LUST-STEVENS-20, VENKATESH-19, LIPNOWSKI-TSIMERMAN-18. The five Part II ids are shared consistently with those extractions (GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII, FiniteFlatGroupsWithTensorsPartII, ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII, ReductiveGroupsIntegralRepresentationsPartII, ReductiveGroupsPartIIGrothendieckSerre; SmoothRepresentationsPartIIParahoricCenters also used by ZHU-17). Searched all atlas stages for local models, parahoric level, affine Grassmannians, affine flag varieties, Kottwitz, Lang and Bernstein centres. Duplications found: findings 10 and 18.

Prerequisites: all 22 entries resolved (20 DOIs through Crossref to the cited works; Anantharaman and Zink via Numdam). Collation: scripts/collation.py classifies the extraction as read from the published text.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-18.result.json: items D08, D09, psi-constant-mod-a, kp18-lemma-3-1-9, D18; gap 'corrections-are-load-bearing'; PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-18.md items table (row D07) and §'corrections'
findings.claim: The review removed item D07 (the corrected first-order comparison of KPZ26 Lemma 5.1.15) as 'Kisin–Pappas–Zhou's, not this paper's', but nothing replaced it. D08 is named 'Versal display deformation with the corrected first-order condition', yet its statement is the printed Lemma 3.1.12: 'if Ψ is constant mod a_R = m_R^2 + pR (in the sense of §3.1.11), then the deformation 𝒢_R of 𝒢_0 is versal', and §3.1.11 (item psi-constant-mod-a) defines that condition through the printed Lemma 3.1.9 isomorphism. E1 (confirmed) says that isomorphism depends on the normal decomposition and that Lemma 3.1.12 does not hold with the printed map; psi-constant-mod-a's own note says the condition is 'not well defined as printed'. So D08, and D09 (whose standing assumption is the same condition) and D18, are stated in the form the authors withdrew, against PROTOCOL §18 ('Items and nodes use the corrected statements'). D08's only prerequisite is D06. Four places still point at the deleted D07: the note of kp18-lemma-3-1-9 ('replaced by KPZ26 Lemma 5.1.15 (the extraction's D07)'), the gap corrections-are-load-bearing ('the items they touch (D07, D08, …) already carry the corrected statements'), and the report's items table (row 'D07 | construction | missing | Corrected relative-frame tilde functor') and corrections paragraph.
findings.evidence: KP18 p. 167, §3.1.11: 'We say that Ψ is constant modulo 𝔞_R if the composite map D̃_1 ⊗_W Ŵ(R/𝔞_R) ≅ M̃_1 ⊗_{Ŵ(R)} Ŵ(R/𝔞_R) → … is equal to Ψ_0 ⊗ 1', the first map being Lemma 3.1.9's. E1 (review verdict confirmed): 'The construction has to be replaced by the one of KPZ26 Lemma 5.1.15', affects 'a stated result'. result.json line 7645 (note of kp18-lemma-3-1-9) and line 8576 (gap) name D07; review notes: 'item D07 removed (its content is Kisin–Pappas–Zhou's, not this paper's)'. The corrected objects exist in the sequel's extraction: PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-ZHOU-26/F10 'Canonical first-order comparison c' (KPZ26 Lemma 5.1.15) and PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-ZHOU-26/psi-constant-modulo-a 'Ψ constant modulo 𝔞 (corrected)' (§5.1.19).
findings.fix: Restate D08 as the corrected lemma: 'if Ψ is constant modulo 𝔞_R in the sense of KPZ26 §5.1.19 (with the canonical c of KPZ26 Lemma 5.1.15), then 𝒢_R is versal', and give it the prerequisites PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-ZHOU-26/F10 and PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-ZHOU-26/psi-constant-modulo-a (imported, not re-planned). Restate D09's standing assumption the same way (or as '𝒢_R versal', all the proof uses), and point D18 and psi-constant-mod-a at the KPZ26 items. Delete the four references to D07 (note of kp18-lemma-3-1-9, the gap, the report table row and paragraph) or replace them by the KPZ26 item ids.

findings.claim: E58 (confirmed) corrects Corollaries 4.2.12 (second sentence) and 4.2.13: the hypothesis must be 𝒢 = 𝒢° (connected special fibre of the stabilizer), not K_p = K_p°. The items were not corrected. S08 reads 'If Kp=Kp°, its geometric special fiber has μ-admissible strata with normal Cohen–Macaulay closures'. S09 keeps 'including K_p = K_p°' as its hypothesis and only adds a parenthesis '(the proof needs 𝒢 = 𝒢°; see the new gap on 4.2.12/4.2.13)', pointing at a 'new gap' that does not exist in `gaps` (it is sourceIssue E58). Under K_p = K_p°, π_0(𝒢_{F_p}) has no nontrivial F_p-points but H^1(F_q, π_0) can be nonzero for q = p^2, so Lang's lemma, used for S09, fails, and the Adm(μ)-strata of S08 need not be 𝒢_k-stable. E58's own example (norm-one torus of Q_p(p^{1/3}), p ≡ 2 mod 3, p > 3: X_*(T)_I = Z/3 with Frobenius acting by −1, so T(Q_p) = 𝒯°(Z_p) although 𝒯 ≠ 𝒯°, and H^1(F_{p^2}, Z/3) ≠ 0) was re-derived.
findings.evidence: KP18 p. 188, Corollary 4.2.12: 'If K_p = K_p°, i.e. K_p is parahoric, then the geometric special fibre 𝒮_K(G,X) ⊗_{O_E} k admits a stratification …'; Corollary 4.2.13: 'Under the above assumptions, including K_p = K_p°, …'; proof: 'Lang's lemma applied to the torsor π_{F_q} for the smooth connected group scheme 𝒢_{F_q}'. E58 correction: 'replace K_p = K_p°, i.e. K_p is parahoric by 𝒢 = 𝒢°, … the hypothesis of KPZ26 Thm. 7.1.3(3)'.
findings.fix: State S08's second sentence and S09 under the hypothesis 𝒢 = 𝒢° (E58), delete the dangling 'see the new gap' reference in S09, and add A02 (Lang) as a prerequisite of S08 as well as S09.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-18.result.json: items S36, S37, S38–S43, S44–S48; sourceIssue E3 (locator); gap 'corrections-are-load-bearing'
findings.claim: The authors' correction that Theorem 4.2.7 needs a very good Hodge embedding (E3, KPZ26 §1.3.1) is carried by S07 only. Nothing in the abelian-type chain supplies one: S38 (Lemma 4.6.22) produces a Hodge-type (G,X) with conditions (1)–(5) and no very good embedding, and S36 (Cor. 4.6.15), S37 (Cor. 4.6.18) and S44–S48 (Thm. 4.6.23) are stated as printed with no very-good hypothesis, although S36 lists S07 as a prerequisite. The gap corrections-are-load-bearing asserts that 'S44–S48 … already carry the corrected statements and the very-good hypothesis'; they do not (for example S47: 'If the adjoint Shimura datum has no D^H factors, choose the cover … Then the model has a Gad° torsor and smooth equivariant local-model map'). On the corrected route the D^H exclusion of S47 is not sufficient: KPZ26 obtains a very good embedding only for non-exceptional data, and the case of 'exceptional type A' factors (Res_{F/Q_p}PGL_m(D), D of index divisible by p) needs KPZ26 Corollary 1.1.3. E3's locator also misses two §4.6 uses of Theorem 4.2.7: the second statement of Corollary 4.6.15 and the last claim of Corollary 4.6.18 (through Lemma 4.5.9).
findings.evidence: KP18 p. 204 (proof of Cor. 4.6.15): 'The second statement then follows from Theorem 4.2.7 and Proposition 4.3.7'; p. 205 (proof of Cor. 4.6.18): 'The final claim can be checked over O_{E^ur}, when it follows easily from Lemma 4.5.9'; p. 208: 'We apply Lemma 4.6.22 and choose (G,X) satisfying conditions (1)–(4) of that Lemma'. KPZ26 (arXiv:2409.03689v3) §1.3.1: '[KP18, Theorem 4.2.7] should be replaced by Theorem 7.1.3 … This affects the final statement [KP18, Theorem 4.6.23] … which should be replaced by Theorem 7.2.21'; §1.3.2: 'Theorem 1.1.2 gives a slightly weaker result in the case that (G^ad, µ^ad) contains factors of "exceptional type A". However, this extra restriction is removed by Corollary 1.1.3'; §6.1 (NE): 'does not contain a simple factor of type D^H, or a simple factor of type A with adjoint group Res_{F/Q_p}PGL_m(D), with D a central division F-algebra of index divisible by p'.
findings.fix: Add to S38 the conclusion of KPZ26 Prop. 7.2.10(3) (the auxiliary datum admits a Hodge embedding extending to a very good one) with its (NE) hypothesis, and make S36, S37, S44–S48 cite the replacement statements (KPZ26 Thm. 7.2.21, and Cor. 1.1.3 for exceptional type A) as their proof route, importing the KPZ26 extraction's items rather than re-planning them. Add Corollary 4.6.15 (second statement, p. 204) and Corollary 4.6.18 (last claim, p. 205) to E3's locator. Correct the sentence of the gap corrections-are-load-bearing. S46 (extension property, by Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich) is unaffected.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-18.result.json: items S47, S48, N06, N14; no item for Theorem 0.4 / Remark 4.6.25(c)
findings.claim: Theorem 0.4, the local model diagram for the abelian-type datum (G,X) with target its own local model M^loc_{G,X} and a 𝒢^{ad°}-torsor, has no item. S47/S48 (Thm. 4.6.23(4),(5)) give the diagram with target the local model of the auxiliary Hodge-type datum (4.6.24); the passage to the abelian-type datum's own local model uses Proposition 2.2.7 (M08) and Remark 4.2.14 (connected-stabilizer-in-unramified-case), which turns the intro's hypothesis 'G unramified and K°_p contained in a hyperspecial' into the hypothesis of (5). §4.7.4 invokes exactly this ('by Theorem 0.4'), and N14 places w in that local model, but N06's prerequisites are S47, S48, N02, A02 and N14's are N06, N10, N13, S45: neither M08 nor connected-stabilizer-in-unramified-case is reached.
findings.evidence: KP18 p. 124, Theorem 0.4: 'Suppose that either (G^ad, X^ad) has no factor of type D^H, or that G is unramified over Q_p and K°_p is contained in a hyperspecial subgroup. Then there exists a local model diagram 𝒮_{K°_p}(G,X) ← 𝒮̃^{ad°}_{K_p} → M^loc_{G,X}, where π is a 𝒢^{ad°}-torsor and q is smooth and 𝒢^{ad°}-equivariant.' p. 210, Remark 4.6.25(c): 'Theorem 0.4 of the Introduction follows from Theorem 4.6.23(4), (5), by using Proposition 2.2.7 and Remark 4.2.14.' p. 213: 'Such a diagram exists when p ∤ |π_1(G^der)| and, either … by Theorem 0.4.'
findings.fix: Add an item 'Theorem 0.4 (Remark 4.6.25(c))' with the intro's hypotheses (p > 2, abelian type, tame, p ∤ |π_1(G^der)|, and either no D^H factor or G unramified with K°_p in a hyperspecial) and conclusion, with prerequisites S47, S48, M08, M07, connected-stabilizer-in-unramified-case and finite-level-quotient-etale-local-structure; route it with S44–S48 (route 9) and make N06 depend on it.

findings.claim: None of the 105 items the review added is a prerequisite of any item, and none has prerequisites of its own: they are isolated from the dependency graph, so the design jobs receive the cited inputs of the proofs without the edges saying which results use them. Examples: G04 (Prop. 1.1.4) has prerequisites G03 and P04 only, though its proof uses steinberg-quasi-split, bt-quasisplit-parahoric-structure, pappas-rapoport-torus-kernel, edixhoven-tame-fixed-points, anantharaman-quotient and bt-big-cell-isomorphism-1-2-13; S46 (Thm. 4.6.23(3)) has only S44, though its proof is siegel-extension-property; S51 (Prop. 4.6.28) lacks toroidal-compactification-hodge-type, milne-extension-property-uniqueness and very-special-irreducible-special-fibre; S38 lacks deligne-hodge-type-lift and sharp-cover-classical-type; M13 lacks gortz-symplectic-local-model; S14 and S49 lack pz-local-model-special-fibre and finite-level-quotient-etale-local-structure. The same result is also recorded three times: G01, haines-rapoport-prop-3 and kottwitz-kernel-and-parahoric-membership all state Haines–Rapoport [38, Prop. 3].
findings.evidence: Computed from the result.json: of the 105 item ids that are not of letter-number form, 105 occur in no item's `prerequisites` list and 105 have an empty `prerequisites` field. KP18 p. 209: 'Then 𝒮_{K'_p}(GSp,S^±) satisfies the extension property in (3), by the Néron-Ogg-Shafarevich criterion'; pp. 128–129 (proof of Prop. 1.1.4) cites Steinberg's theorem, [11, §4.4, §4.6], [1, §4] and the big cell; pp. 127–128 (§1.1.2) and p. 180 both cite '[38, Prop. 3]'.
findings.fix: Wire each added item into the graph: give it its own prerequisites and add it to the prerequisites of the items whose proofs cite it (at least the edges listed in the claim). Merge G01, haines-rapoport-prop-3 and kottwitz-kernel-and-parahoric-membership into one item with the locators §1.1.2 (pp. 127–128), p. 180 and pp. 189–190.

findings.claim: The paper's ambient projective spaces have no item: the Grassmannian Gr(V_{Z_p}) over Z_p (Cor. 2.3.16, and the Siegel moduli of §4.1), the Lagrangian Grassmannian LGr(V) (§2.3.4, (2.3.6)), and the flag variety X_μ = G/P_{μ^{-1}} over E (§2.1.1, M02). The atlas plans Grassmannians and flag schemes: AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.1 ('Construct projective bundles, Grassmannians and flag schemes with their quotient/subbundle universal properties'), and the reviewed library audit marks Mathlib's Module.Grassmannian as partial (functor of points only; representability is a TODO). findings.claim: The semisimple trace is defined without saying which Frobenius, and Theorem 4.7.11 is true only for the geometric Frobenius. N02 writes 'Tr^ss(Frob, V) = Σ_i Tr(Frob, (gr_i V)^{I_E})' and N06/N14 'Trss(Froby, …)'. The paper's source for the trace, Pappas–Zhu, fixes σ to be the geometric Frobenius. Check: GL_2 with Iwahori level (the Γ_0(p) model, semistable). At a crossing point the nearby-cycle stalk has H^0 = Q̄_ℓ and H^1 = Q̄_ℓ(−1), with inertia acting unipotently and trivially on the graded pieces. The geometric Frobenius acts on Q̄_ℓ(−1) by q, so Tr^ss = 1 − q, the value of q^{1/2} z_μ on the length-zero double coset; the arithmetic Frobenius gives 1 − q^{-1}, and (4.7.12) fails. At hyperspecial level both give 1, which hides the problem. Route 10's brief already asks for 'geometric Frobenius' in z_{μ,r}, so the items and the brief disagree.
findings.evidence: KP18 p. 212: 'one can define [62] the semi-simple trace of Frobenius Tr^ss(Frob_x, RΨ(X,ℱ)_x̄)' (no convention given). Pappas–Zhu arXiv:1110.5588v4 §9.d, p. 75: Tr^ss(σ, V) … 'where σ is the geometric Frobenius element' (this is the extraction's pz13 archive, SHA-256 cbb87912…, re-fetched). KP18 p. 214, (4.7.12): 'Tr^ss(Frob_y, RΨ^𝒮_ȳ) = q^{d/2} z_{μ,r}(w)'.
findings.fix: In N02 define Tr^ss with σ the geometric Frobenius (PZ v4 §9.d.1), and say in N06 and N14 that Frob_y and Frob_w are geometric Frobenius elements.

findings.claim: The proof of Proposition 4.3.7 uses that prime-to-p level change 𝒮_{K'} → 𝒮_K on the normalized models is finite étale, citing Proposition 4.2.2; no item states this, and S14's prerequisites are only S10, S12, S13. Proposition 4.2.2 is one of the results E3 says needs a very good embedding, and the review of E3 keeps 4.3.7 only because 'normalization commutes with finite étale change of prime-to-p level', an argument that exists only in a review note. The deduction also needs 𝒮_{K'°} → 𝒮_{K°} to be étale and surjective, since a composite of étale maps factoring through 𝒮_{K°} does not by itself make 𝒮_{K°} → 𝒮_K étale.
findings.evidence: KP18 p. 191 (proof of Prop. 4.3.7): 'Then, by what we have shown above together with Proposition 4.2.2, the maps 𝒮_{K'°}(G,X) → 𝒮_{K'}(G,X) → 𝒮_K(G,X) are finite étale. Since the composite of these maps factors through 𝒮_{K°}(G,X), it follows that 𝒮_{K°}(G,X) → 𝒮_K(G,X) is finite étale.' E3 review note: 'Proposition 4.3.7 is left out: its use of 4.2.2 is replaceable, since normalization commutes with finite étale change of prime-to-p level'.

findings.claim: E17 is right but its reason can be sharpened, and two items are loose. (a) The step 'H^1(𝒦, G) = {1}' of Lemma 1.4.6 is not merely unsupported for finite k, it is false: for p odd and G the split G_2 (quasi-split, simply connected, no E_8), with ε ∈ W^× lifting a non-square of k, the 3-fold Pfister form ⟨⟨ε, u, p⟩⟩ is anisotropic over the completion ℰ of 𝒦 at (p) (Springer's theorem twice: residues ⟨⟨ε̄, u⟩⟩ over k((u)), then ⟨1, −ε̄⟩ over k), so H^1(𝒦, G_2) ≠ 1. Whether the lemma's conclusion H^1(D[1/p], G) = 1 fails for finite k remains open. (b) U04 says that for finite k 'these values are 3' for both cd_ℓ and cd_p; Hu 2013 Theorem 4.5, which it cites, covers ℓ ≠ p only, and only cd(𝒦) ≥ 3 is needed. (c) U06 omits that Step 2 of Proposition 1.4.3 is in the case k algebraically closed; that is what makes the tame splitting field cyclic, and for finite k the biquadratic K_0(√ε, √p)/K_0 is tame and not cyclic.
findings.evidence: KP18 p. 145: 'Set 𝒦 = Frac(W[[u]]). This is a field of cohomological dimension 2 … Therefore, H^1(𝒦, G) = {1}'; p. 146: 'Since we are assuming that G splits after a tamely ramified (and hence cyclic) extension of K_0 the flasque torus Z is also a direct summand of an induced torus (see [14, Prop. 1] …)'.
findings.fix: Add the G_2 counterexample to E17's reason and say that the lemma is unproved, not known false, for finite k. In U04 write 'cd(𝒦) ≥ 3 for finite k (= 3 for ℓ ≠ p by Hu 2013, Thm. 4.5)'. In U06 add 'k algebraically closed (so the tame splitting field is cyclic)'.
